title: UpsertFrameworkAgreement
description: A framework agreement as a first-class entity, keyed by the framework's own grouping key rather than by any one notice, so every award notice that belongs to the framework converges on one node — which the per-notice UpsertContract cannot do. Sinks materialise ESTABLISHED (Authority→FrameworkAgreement) from buyer_authority_id, PARTY_TO {lot, rank} (Company→FrameworkAgreement) from suppliers, and CALL_OFF_OF (Contract→FrameworkAgreement) from UpsertContract.framework_id. The ESTABLISHED / CALL_OFF_OF edge names are historical: nothing in the data tells the notice that set the framework up from one that draws on it, so a reader shows the cluster as 'part of a framework agreement' and never as establishment-then-call-offs. Aggregation rule: the ceiling is capacity, not spend — framework nodes never enter spend sums; contracts do.

framework_id.description: Identity of the framework = the normalised eForms OPT-100 Framework Notice Identifier, the grouping key every award notice of the framework carries: a TED publication number with zero-padding stripped ('536632-2024') or an eForms notice UUID without its '-NN' version suffix. It is NOT the establishing procedure's contract key — OPT-100 names a notice in the same ContractFolderID only 53.5% of the time, a different folder 17.2%, and legacy targets have no folder at all. Contracts reference it as UpsertContract.framework_id; the notice it names is usually a call-for-competition this platform does not ingest, so it identifies the framework without resolving to a contract we hold.

buyer_authority_id.description: authority_id of the contracting authority (or central purchasing body) on the notice this event was built from. Sinks materialise ESTABLISHED from it; the edge name is historical — the data does not confirm that this notice established the framework.

establishing_notice_id.description: ted_notice_id of the notice these terms were read from (the eForms notice UUID, or the legacy notice id) — provenance for the node; identity is framework_id. Despite the name it is not evidence of establishment: every award notice of a framework carries the same OPT-100 key and none of them says which one set the framework up.

country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code of the establishing authority.

ceiling_eur.description: Maximum value of the framework in EUR (eForms BT-118 / BT-709, converted at the establishing notice's publication date). Capacity, never spend: readers show call-off spend consumed against it and no aggregate sums it.

ceiling_currency.description: Original ISO 4217 currency of the ceiling before EUR conversion.

ceiling_original.description: The ceiling in the original currency.

reestimated_value_eur.description: Re-estimated value of the framework in EUR (eForms BT-660): the buyer's later expectation of what will actually be called off, distinct from the ceiling.

duration_start.description: Start of the framework's validity period (ISO date).

duration_end.description: End of the framework's validity period (ISO date). Call-offs published after it are still attached; the date is what the reader shows, not a filter.

duration_months.description: Duration in months (eForms BT-36 normalised to months) when the notice gives a duration rather than dates; both forms may be present.

cpv.description: Primary CPV code of the framework.

lot_count.description: Number of lots the framework covers.

supplier_count.description: Number of economic operators admitted to the framework as published by this notice (eForms: one SettledContract per framework supplier). May exceed the length of suppliers when some were withheld by the cleaning stage or not resolved.

suppliers.description: Every economic operator admitted to the framework (the PARTY_TO set). Multi-supplier is the normal case; admission is not a call-off award, so no value is carried here — call-off spend lives on the call-off contracts.

company_gmr_id.description: Resolved company gmr_id of the admitted operator.

lot.description: Lot identifier the operator is admitted for (eForms 'LOT-0001' style); null when the framework is single-lot or the notice does not say.

rank.description: cbc:RankCode within the lot's cascade when published; null otherwise.
